audit.whatIsWrong: The chart on disk read Skill / Ornn / Ornn / Skill / Skill / Ornn / Ornn. The mirror audit (aurora__ornn) already committed to Ornn / Ornn / Skill / Skill / Ornn / Ornn / Ornn, which is also the packet chart and what this page's own whys describe.
audit.why: Level 1 is Ornn's — Aurora has no poke online and a squishy body. Level 3 is genuinely skill: Searing Charge into the pillar wins unless she holds a blink. Level 6 is Ornn's — the Call of the Forge God recast cannot be blinked once it is travelling through her.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 3 and 5 flipped in matched full/content pairs to agree with the mirror; ratings moved with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why was boilerplate and hedged on 'Aurora's ultimate'.
audit.why: Between Worlds is a leap, shockwave and slow zone, not an all-in answer to a charging knockup. Call of the Forge God's charge plus recast is the stronger 6.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states the charge, the recast ram and why she cannot blink out of it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tracked 'Twofold Hex (Blink)' as Aurora's escape. Twofold Hex is her Q — a 900-range curse missile with a recast. Her blink is Across the Veil (W), 22s at rank 1; The Weirding (E) is the 15s backward hop. Spirit Abjuration's healing was never mentioned.
audit.why: The whole tracking hook was pointed at the wrong ability, so the advice to 'engage when it is down' was keyed to a 9s poke spell instead of the 22s blink. Searing Charge is 14s against that 22s, which is the real asymmetry to play around. Spirit Abjuration heals her off every damaging hit, so Grievous Wounds timing matters in extended trades.
audit.corrected: focus.text, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[0]/[1] now use the right names, the 22s vs 14s asymmetry, Twofold Hex's 900 range, and the passive heal.

edits.before: Q-poke and AA-trade — your base stats are quietly elite. Identify how Aurora contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Aurora has no poke online turn 1 and a squishy body — step up, Bellows Breath her through the minions, and win the exchange.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Aurora must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Searing Charge into your own pillar wins the trade, but a held Across the Veil blinks her off the telegraph — skill on skill.

edits.before: Call of the Forge God re-engages a whole fight — and your forge prints item leads. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Aurora's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Call of the Forge God charges her down and the recast rams her a second time — she cannot blink that once it is travelling through her. Your window.

edits.before: - Aurora Twofold Hex: matchup-defining — Her escape. E-knock up around it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Across the Veil: her blink, 22s at rank 1 — Searing Charge is 14s, so you get a free commit every other one. - The Weirding: 15s backward hop. - Twofold Hex: 9s poke. - Your R: kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Aurora's Twofold Hex before you commit
edits.after: Track Aurora's Across the Veil before you commit

edits.before: Her escape. E-knock up around it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Across the Veil is 22s and your Searing Charge 14s — commit on her blink.

edits.before: Aurora wastes Twofold Hex (Blink) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Aurora spends Across the Veil — commit the full pattern immediately.

edits.before: That is Aurora's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Twofold Hex out-ranges you at 900 and its recast hits again — walk her down instead.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Spirit Abjuration heals her off every hit — bring Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: E-dashing with no terrain in the line — no knockup means you delivered yourself to his combo for free.
edits.after: She stays squishy and never out-scales you — take the free plates and let Masterwork upgrades close it.

edits.before: Q the pillar behind Aurora, E-dash through it for the knockup when his answer is down, and W-brittle the trade for the proc.
edits.after: Drop the Q pillar behind Aurora, Searing Charge into it for the knockup, then Bellows Breath to Brittle and burst her.

notes: The tracked ability was wrong for the whole matchup: 'Twofold Hex (Blink)' treated her 900-range Q poke missile as her escape. Her blink is Across the Veil (W, 22s). Following the mirror audit, nothing here claims Volcanic Rupture grounds anything — Riot's Q text says damage, slow and pillar only. Still unresolved from the kits and not asserted: whether Between Worlds' repositioning can be used to leave an already-landed knockup.
